title: Protocol for serial organoid formation assay using primary colorectal cancer tissues to evaluate cancer stem cell activity
protocol: Obtain patient-derived samples with informed consent.
Mechanically dissociate freshly resected human colorectal tumor tissues into smaller fragments.
Enzymatically dissociate the tissue fragments.
Strain the resulting cell suspension to eliminate debris and aggregates.
Lysis red blood cells in the cell suspension.
Exclude dead cells from the suspension.
Apply a sorting procedure to isolate the CD133+ fraction.
Culture the isolated CD133+ fraction in non-adherent conditions to initiate spheroid formation.
Preserve fresh primary colorectal tumor tissues on ice in a 15 mL conical tube containing physiological saline solution such as PBS.
Proceed immediately to tissue dissociation in a biological safety cabinet after obtaining a freshly resected primary CRC sample in a 50 mL collection tube on ice.
Transfer the CRC tumor fragment to a 35 mm petri dish containing 5 mL of ice-cold phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) solution.
Use PBS to wash blood and/or debris from the tumor fragment.
Aspirate the PBS and perform a second wash using 3 mL of cold CSC media.
Aspirate again and replace the media with 3 mL of fresh CSC media.
Dissect the tissue into multiple fractions for protein/RNA/DNA extracts or histology embedding if biobanking is advised.
Preserve a tissue section of ≥1 cm³ for CSC isolation.
Utilize forceps to immobilize the tumor fragment.
Use a razor blade to mince the tumor fragment into ∼2 mm pieces in CSC media.
Cut the aspirating end of a p1000 tip using scissors to make it wider.
Transfer minced tumor fragment suspension to a 50 mL conical tube containing 5 mL of Tumor Dissociation Solution.
Incubate the tube in a 37°C incubator or water bath for 1 h.
Vigorously flick the tube 10–15 times every 15 min during incubation.
Alternatively, perform 10–15 up and down pipetting with a sterile 5 mL serological pipette every 15 min.
Pass the digested tumor suspension through a sterile 70 μm cell strainer into a new sterile 50 mL conical tube.
Wash the strainer with 1–2 mL of CSC media to collect any remaining cells.
Centrifuge the filtrate at 450×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Extend centrifugation time if no substantial cell pellet is observed.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant from the tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL of a solution of 0.8% (w/v) Ammonium Chloride 0.8% + 0.1 mM EDTA to lyse red blood cells.
Incubate on ice for 10 min to allow red blood cell lysis.
If necessary, increase the volume of Ammonium Chloride solution and let the cells deposit for an extra 10 min if red blood cell lysis is incomplete.
Add an equal volume of CSC media to the cell suspension after red blood cell lysis.
Centrifuge at 450×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of fresh CSC media.
Remove dead cells from the tumor cell suspension using Ficoll or a Dead Cell Removal kit following manufacturer’s guidelines.
Resuspend the resulting live cell fraction into desired volume of CSC media.
Perform cell viability counts using trypan blue and a hemocytometer, or an automated cell counter.
Proceed to Magnetic-Activated Cell Sorting (MACS) of the primary CRC cell suspension.
Obtain a fraction enriched in CD133+ tumor-initiating cells.
Use the MiniMACS Starting Kit with the CD133 MicroBead Kit according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Maintain robust CSC-enriched spheroids in suspension.
Monitor spheroid cultures daily.
Change CSC media at least once every 3 days.
Place flasks containing spheroid cultures in a sterile biological safety cabinet.
Transfer the entire volume to a 15 mL conical tube.
Allow spheres to deposit at the bottom of the tube.
Proceed to a brief, gentle centrifugation (450×g, 30 seconds) if necessary.
Aspirate the culture media without disturbing the pellet.
Resuspend spheroids in 8–10 mL of fresh CSC media gently.
Passage CSC-enriched spheroid cultures once a week or earlier if fast growth is observed.
Mechanically disrupt spheroids using vigorous up and down pipetting for 5 minutes with a sterile 5 mL serological pipette.
Transfer the spheroids suspension to a 15 mL conical tube using a sterile 10 mL serological pipette.
Separate larger cultures into two tubes if necessary to ensure ease of disruption.
Filter the cell suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer.
Resuspend the filtered cell suspension in CSC media.
Perform cell counts to determine the concentration.
Transfer 5 × 10^4 cells/mL into 8 mL of CSC media in non-adherent culture flasks.
Freeze stocks at early passages in freezing media consisting of 10% DMSO, 30% KnockOut Serum Replacement, and 60% CSC media mixture.
Thaw frozen spheroids immediately by washing off the freezing media with fresh CSC media.
Resuspend thawed spheroids gently in fresh CSC media to minimize disruption of structures.
Track the number of passages to avoid exceeding 10–12 passages for each culture.
Optional: Use enzymatic dissociation as an alternative method for passaging, but be aware it can affect surface protein markers and alter experimental readouts.
Transfer CSC-enriched spheroids from culture flasks to 15 mL conical tubes.
Mechanically dissociate the spheres to generate single-cell suspensions.
Pass the dissociated spheroid suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer to eliminate multicellular aggregates.
Perform viral vector-based transduction on the single cell suspension prior to BME embedding if required.
Take an aliquot of BME from -80°C and let it thaw on ice.
Perform a live cell count using trypan blue and a hemocytometer or an automated cell counter.
Dilute cells in CSC media to a concentration of 2 cells/μL.
Transfer 900 μL of the cell suspension into a sterile 15 mL conical tube.
Add 900 μL of BME to the cell suspension for a final dilution of 1 cell/μL.
Gently homogenize the BME/cell mixture with a p1000 pipettor.
Deposit 300 μL of the BME/cell mixture at the center of each well in a 6-well culture plate.
Dispense BME volume in the center of the well using a p1000 pipettor.
Avoid any disturbances such as shocks or excessive vibrations during and after plating.
Carefully dispense the remainder of the 300 μL at the same position to form a tridimensional dome.
Ensure the dome does not spread out along the plate.
Place lid on the culture plate without disrupting the domes.
Gently transfer the plate to the incubator for a 10-min incubation at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Transfer the dome-containing plate back to the biological safety cabinet once the polymerization period is over.
Visually inspect each well under a light microscope after 10 minutes at 37°C to ensure an even vertical distribution of cells across the dome structures.
Fill the dome-containing wells with 3 mL of CSC media.
Initiate drug treatments (or controls) ≥24 hours post-seeding by adding the appropriate concentration of each compound in a fresh batch of CSC media, using 3 mL per well.
Carefully aspirate the media from dome-containing wells without disrupting the structures.
Add 3 mL of drug or control/vehicle supplemented CSC media to the dome-containing wells.
Replace the media with fresh, drug-free CSC media at the desired period to terminate drug treatments.
Extend tumor organoid growth periods beyond the drug treatments as desired.
Use a high content imaging system to quantify changes in organoid counts and other morphological characteristics, such as size and form factor, in response to drug treatments.
Perform brightfield scans of each well with Z-stack acquisition using a 4× or 10× objective.
Identify and count CRC tumor organoids based on a size exclusion threshold approach.
Harvest BME-embedded primary organoids.
Dissociate primary organoids into single-cell suspensions.
Embed dissociated cells in a secondary series of BME domes.
Do not expose the secondary series to any drug treatments or other therapeutic interventions.
Take an aliquot of BME out from -80°C and let it thaw on ice.
Gently aspirate the media surrounding the primary organoid-containing domes.
Wash each well with 4 mL of sterile PBS.
Discard the PBS by gently aspirating.
Add 1 mL of Gentle Cell Dissociation reagent to chemically dissociate the BME domes and organoids.
Transfer the plate(s) containing the organoids to the incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 10 min.
Pipette up and down using a sterile 5 mL serological pipette after the first 5 min of incubation.
Put the plate back to the incubator for another 5 min.
Execute up and down pipetting until no organoids are visible once the 10-min incubation is over.
Filter the cell suspension through a 70 μm strainer to eliminate multicellular aggregates.
Collect the filtrate in a new sterile 50 mL conical tube.
Complete the filtrate volume to 10 mL with CSC media.
Perform cell counts using trypan blue and a hemocytometer, or an automated cell counter.
Plate a total of 15 × 10^4 cells in a volume of 300 μL of BME:cell suspension mixture (or 50 cells/μL) for each secondary dome.
